item.title: China's yuan loans grow 11.42 trln yuan in first 10 months
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China's yuan loans grow 11.42 trln yuan in first 10 months BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China's yuan-denominated loans rose by 11.42 trillion yuan (about 1.7 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first 10 months of 2026, central bank data showed on Friday. At the end of October, outstanding yuan loans stood at 283.33 trillion yuan, up 4.7 percent year on year, according to the People's Bank of China (PBOC). China's outstanding aggregate financing to the real economy stood at 469.16 trillion yuan at the end of October, up 7.2 percent year on year, the central bank noted. M2, a broad measure of money supply that covers cash in circulation and all deposits, increased by 7.1 percent year on year to 359.06 trillion yuan by the end of last month, the PBOC said. "Growth rates of M2 and total social financing remained at reasonable levels, creating an appropriate monetary and financial environment for economic recovery and upgrading," said Zhou Zhen, associate professor at Tsinghua University's PBC School of Finance. Credit has flowed increasingly to key areas. In the first 10 months, loans to enterprises and public institutions increased by 12.39 trillion yuan, including 6.69 trillion yuan in medium- and long-term loans. Outstanding inclusive loans to small and micro businesses rose 6.9 percent year on year to 38.24 trillion yuan. Outstanding medium- and long-term loans to the service sector, excluding the real estate sector, rose 9.2 percent to 62.99 trillion yuan. Both outpaced overall loan growth. By the end of September, some 307,300 small and medium-sized sci-tech enterprises had received loan support, with a loan access rate of 51.1 percent. Financing channels have become more diversified. In the first 10 months, bond and equity financing accounted for around 53 percent of new aggregate social financing. Funding costs remained low this year. In October, the weighted average rate on newly issued enterprise loans was about 2.9 percent, down 0.2 percentage points year on year, while that on new personal housing loans was about 3.1 percent, basically unchanged from the same period last year. Zhang Xu, an analyst at Everbright Securities, said that as the integrated effects of existing and new policies continue to emerge, the financial system will keep providing strong support for the high-quality development of the real economy. item.title: China expects greater consensus, more tangible outcomes with APEC parties: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China expects greater consensus, more tangible outcomes with APEC parties: spokesperson BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China looks forward to building further consensus among parties of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), achieving more tangible outcomes, and injecting robust impetus into prosperity and growth in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said on Friday. Spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing when answering a query related to the upcoming 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Noting that after 12 years, China is once again hosting APEC, Mao said the APEC "China Year" has yielded fruitful outcomes. China has successfully held over 300 meetings and events by focusing on the theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" and the three priority areas of "Openness, Innovation, and Cooperation." More than 10,000 representatives have participated in the events and reached a number of common understandings on cooperation, laying a solid foundation for the upcoming meeting, said the spokesperson. With this APEC meeting set to open next week, Mao said China looks forward to agreeing on the APEC Shenzhen Leaders' Declaration among all member economies as well as more practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, and artificial intelligence. item.title: China's top diplomat meets U.S. representatives attending political dialogue
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China's top diplomat meets U.S. representatives attending political dialogue Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, meets with U.S. representatives attending the U.S.-China Political Dialogue 2026 in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu) BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- China's top diplomat Wang Yi on Friday met with U.S. representatives attending the U.S.-China Political Dialogue 2026 in Beijing. Wang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, said that China and the United States should clarify the goals of their joint efforts, expand the areas of mutually beneficial cooperation, consolidate the foundation of bilateral relations, and be committed to maintaining world peace and stability. The two sides should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation, and implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state on building a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, Wang noted. The representative of the U.S. side said that people-to-people and cultural exchanges, especially those between young people and students, are conducive to enhancing friendship and mutual trust between the two peoples, adding that they are grateful for the invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study in the coming five years, and are willing to make efforts to promote the healthy and stable development of U.S.-China relations. item.title: China willing to further boost political mutual trust with Thailand, says Chinese premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-14
China willing to further boost political mutual trust with Thailand, says Chinese premier Chinese Premier Li Qiang holds talks with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok, Thailand, Nov. 13, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) BANGKOK, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Friday that China is willing to work with Thailand to further consolidate the foundation of political mutual trust, support each other's core interests and major concerns, tap cooperation potential in various fields and deliver more tangible results to better benefit the peoples of both countries. Li made the remarks when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. He said Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Anutin during the Thai PM's official visit to China in July, and the two leaders jointly charted the course for the development of China-Thailand relations. Li said that, with his visit to Thailand, the prime ministers of the two countries have exchanged visits within four months, fully demonstrating the high level of bilateral relations. Noting that both China and Thailand are at an important stage of national development, Li said China firmly supports the Thai government in smoothly carrying out its work. China is willing to work with Thailand to make good use of mechanisms such as the "2+2" strategic dialogue between foreign and defense ministers and the joint committee on economic and trade cooperation, Li said. China stands ready to work with Thailand to strengthen the alignment of development strategies, advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and key projects such as the China-Thailand railway, and accelerate consultations on a new five-year plan for economic and trade cooperation, Li said. He added that China is ready to promote the early realization of mutual protection of geographical indication products, and expand cooperation in such fields as finance, new energy, semiconductors, and artificial intelligence, so as to achieve mutual benefit and win-win outcomes at a higher level. China is ready to import more quality products from Thailand and encourages Chinese companies to invest and do business in the Southeast Asian country, he said, adding that China hopes the Thai side will provide a fair, stable and predictable business environment for Chinese companies. The two sides, Li said, should also strengthen exchanges and cooperation in areas including disaster prevention and mitigation, water resources management, education, tourism and media, and step up efforts to combat illegal and criminal activities, to enhance the people's sense of gain from China-Thailand cooperation. At present, the international situation remains fraught with instability and uncertainty, Li said, noting that China is willing to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Thailand under multilateral frameworks including China-ASEAN, the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation, the United Nations, the World Trade Organization and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, so as to contribute to global peace and development. For his part, Anutin said Thailand attaches great importance to its relations with China and is committed to advancing all-round cooperation between the two countries and continuously elevating the Thailand-China comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership to new heights, bringing greater benefits to the two peoples. Thailand is willing to strengthen high-level exchanges with China, make good use of mechanisms such as the "2+2" strategic dialogue between foreign and defense ministers of the two countries, expand bilateral trade, and deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in fields including agriculture, finance, connectivity, electric vehicles, artificial intelligence, e-commerce, and science and technology, said the Thai prime minister. Thailand is ready to continue providing a favorable business environment for Chinese enterprises investing in Thailand, strengthen law enforcement and security cooperation with China to combat online gambling, telecom and online fraud among other crimes, ensure the safety of Chinese tourists, and deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges to consolidate the foundation of public friendship, Anutin said. Thailand supports China's successful hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and stands ready to work with China to ensure the success of the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Leaders' Meeting, making new contributions to regional stability, development and prosperity, said the Thai prime minister. Following the talks, the two leaders witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the fields including the automotive industry, vocational education, agriculture, customs and security. item.title: Tennis gains fresh momentum in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Tennis gains fresh momentum in China Spectators pack the stands at the 2026 China Open in Beijing. (Photo from the official website of the China Open) As the Guangzhou Open drew to a close, the China tennis season entered its final stretch. Now in its second year as a branded series, the season included eight international professional tournaments at different levels across multiple cities, creating a tennis festival that lasted nearly two months. Breakthrough performances by Chinese players, closer integration of sports, culture, tourism, and commerce, and greater global exposure for China's stories all contributed to the season's outstanding performance. Throughout the season, Chinese players competed across the country, delivering one surprise after another. China's Zheng Qinwen captured the women's singles title at the 2026 China Open, becoming the first Chinese woman to win the title in the tournament's 20-year history. After undergoing elbow surgery and seeing her world ranking plunge, Zheng faced down outside criticism and fought her way back. "I am just so grateful that I found the inner fire back. Right now, I'm trying to reach the best version of myself," she said. Her journey from a difficult period of injury recovery to winning her maiden WTA 1000 crown on home soil is a testament to her resilience. Zheng Qinwen competes at the China Open in Beijing. (Photo from the official website of the China Open) Beyond the excitement on court, tournaments in the China tennis season have become important driving forces of consumption and economic growth, while tennis is becoming a popular lifestyle choice. The China Open set new records for both attendance and consumer spending. More than 450,000 spectator visits were recorded during the tournament, with spectators from outside Beijing accounting for 60 percent. Ticket revenue reached 132 million yuan (about $19.78 million), while related consumer spending surpassed 55 million yuan, both hitting record highs. Sales of licensed merchandise doubled from a year earlier. The influx of spectators gave a boost to consumer spending across the city. The Shanghai Masters extended the tournament experience beyond the courts, creating diverse settings and opportunities for people to experience tennis in different parts of the city. This year, it launched a carnival featuring open training sessions, a tennis-themed museum, and celebrity exhibition matches beyond regular match hours. "The tournament is no longer confined to a single venue. Through innovative activities such as a citywide stamp collecting activity, and combined tickets for multiple tournaments, we are bringing the excitement of tennis into neighborhoods across the city, extending the value of the tournament brand, and unlocking the potential for high-end consumption," said Yang Yibin, chairman of Shanghai Juss Sports and Entertainment Group. This year's tournament attracted nearly 250,000 spectator visits, around 12 percent of whom came from overseas. Total revenue reached approximately 500 million yuan, with sponsorship, ticket sales, and revenue from TV broadcasting rights sharing all hitting record highs. The Wuhan Open in Wuhan, central China's Hubei province, teamed up with shopping areas and scenic areas to offer exclusive discounts to ticket holders, connecting the tournament with tourism resources across the province. It attracted a record 202,700 spectator visits, hitting a new high. The tournament generated an estimated 890 million yuan in overall economic benefits, up 26.24 percent from the previous year. The Chengdu Open ran dedicated shuttle buses between the tournament venue and shopping areas around the city. On board, spectators could find shopping guides and scan QR codes to access ticket-holder offers. By showing their match tickets, they could enjoy discounts and special offers on dining, shopping, culture and tourism experience at nearly 3,000 businesses across the city. Tennis enjoys global appeal, and the China tennis season provides a platform for exchange. Beyond the courts, international players can experience Chinese culture firsthand and share their stories of China with audiences around the world. Elena Rybakina, the world No. 1 in women's singles, experiences Chinese culture at the Yuebo Academy by Dongqian Lake in Ningbo, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo courtesy of the Dongqian Lake scenic area) During the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, the Hangzhou Open organized a nighttime cruise on West Lake aboard the "Moon Boat," offering players a close-up experience of traditional Chinese music, classical dance and the romantic charm of worshipping the moon. Ahead of the Ningbo Open, Elena Rybakina, the world No. 1 in women's singles, visited the Yuebo Academy by Dongqian Lake. Dressed in Song Dynasty (960-1279) attire, she tried her hand at traditional tea making and painting oil-paper umbrellas. Spanish player Alejandro Davidovich Fokina visited a Shu brocade cultural and creative park in Chengdu, where he watched the intricate process of weaving the traditional fabric on a drawloom. He said: "Tennis is all about rhythm and patience, while every inch of this brocade reflects a dedication passed down through generations." On and off the court, more and more foreign players, referees and technical officials have learned to exchange greetings in Chinese. Chinese spectators, meanwhile, have won widespread praise from players for their spectator etiquette. What has made an especially deep impression are the thoughtful gifts from Chinese fans, including hand-drawn portraits of tennis stars, handwritten letters of support and city-themed souvenirs. After winning the China Open, Serbian tennis star Novak Djokovic said: "Chinese fans are among the best in the world. They bring me all kinds of gifts and wait for me for so long. Their thoughtfulness is truly touching." Bai Xilin, director of the Tennis Administration Center of China's General Administration of Sport, said the China tennis season demonstrates the sport's value on multiple fronts. "More and more people are coming to tennis tournaments not just for the matches, but also to experience the culture and emotional connections they offer," he said. item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.
